$comment: VAPP-85: the `Box` style whitelist, verbatim from the VAPP-4 spike (`vapp_spike::WHITELIST` + the logical inline properties the spike added), extended by round 1 (docs/round-1-contract.md) — ONE source for the TS keys (`src/style.ts`), the JSON Schema (`core.schema.json#/$defs/style`) and the Swift/Kotlin/Rust key lists. Numbers are px (≡ pt ≡ dp); `length` also takes `"N%"`, `"Npx"` and `"auto"`; every value may be a token reference `$<group>.<name>` from tokens.json; a COLOUR (`backgroundColor`, `color`, `borderColor`, gradient stops) is ONLY a `$color.<name>` token (round 4, VAPP-103: a literal `#hex` ignores the theme's light and dark modes, so validateStyle refuses it; themes keep literals). `borderWidth` and the four per-side widths are the visual keys with layout effect (a number or `$border.<name>`, VAPP-92); `fontFamily` (VAPP-92) takes only `$type.family.<name>`; `transition` takes only `$motion.<name>` (the duration every opacity/colour/transform/size change animates with; nothing animates without it) and `transitionEasing` only `$ease.<name>`; `transform` is PAINT-ONLY (`translate(Xpx, Ypx)`, `scale(N)`, `rotate(Ndeg)`, space-separated, never layout); `backgroundGradient` = `{angle, stops: [{color, offset 0..1}]}` painted OVER `backgroundColor` (CSS order: the colour shows only through transparent stops); `visibility: hidden` keeps the box in layout and paints nothing (`display: none` removes it); `cursor` is a pointer-platform hint touch platforms ignore. CONDITIONS nest one level and apply in SOURCE ORDER after the base (write narrow-first): `@media` keys match the ONE grammar in `conditions.media` — `min-width`/`max-width`/`min-height`/`max-height` against the SURFACE box (`min-*` = `size >= N`, `max-*` = `size < N`; `N` = px or a `$breakpoint.<name>` token the theme resolves BEFORE matching), `orientation` of the surface box, `hover: hover|none` = a hover-capable pointer, `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce|no-preference` from the platform; the state keys `:hover`, `:focus-visible`, `:pressed` against the node's own interaction state, applied after every media block in that order (pressed wins). `src/style.ts resolveConditions` is the reference flattening and fixtures/style-conditions.json locks it. Still not in v1 (confirmed by the spike, kept by round 1): calc(), named grid lines, gridAutoFlow, justifyItems, order, zIndex (paint order = tree order, absolute nodes LAST among siblings, overlays stack by LAYER), per-side border colours (gpui paints ONE border colour per box; per-side WIDTHS are in), multi-value shorthands. After macro expansion a style VALUE may be a binding or a function call (a bound macro input, e.g. Progress fill width = percent{…}); the renderer resolves it at bind time and then applies it like an authored value; authors cannot write one (validateStyle refuses). Round 2 (docs/round-2-contract.md §2): `position: sticky` = relative in layout, then pinned inside the nearest scrolling ancestor (`overflow` scroll/auto, else the surface scroller) by its `top`/`bottom`/`left`/`right`/`inset*` offsets while its parent is in view; `backdropBlur` takes only `$blur.<name>` (blurs what is BEHIND the box through its translucent background; a platform without backdrop blur paints the background alone, so pair it with a translucent `backgroundColor`); `animation` names a keyframe set of `animations` (`animationDuration` = `$motion.<name>` only); `direction` may sit on ANY node and is inherited (flex rows, logical insets/paddings, `textAlign` start/end and mirrored glyphs follow the node's resolved direction).

animations.$comment: Round 2 (docs/round-2-contract.md §2): the keyframes behind the `animation` key. Channels: `opacity` (multiplies the node's), `translateX`/`translateY` (px), `rotate` (deg), `scale`, applied OUTSIDE the node's own `transform` about the box centre; `band` = the shimmer highlight's position across the box (-1 = one box width before it, 1 = one after), painted over the content and clipped to the border box. Duration = the theme's `duration` token (or the node's `animationDuration`) × `factor`; `easing` applies PER keyframe segment (CSS) and is a `$ease` token or `linear`; `iterations` = a count or `infinite`. An animation starts when the node enters the tree (first paint, `visible` turning true, a template item appearing). Reduced motion: no animation, the node shows the keyframe at `rest` (0 = the first, 1 = the last; shimmer draws no band). Channels are PHYSICAL, like `transform`: `direction` never mirrors them (in rtl too, `slide-in-left` moves leftwards and the shimmer band sweeps left → right).

textShimmer.$comment: EXP-1324: the Text `shimmer` prop (a running TraceItem title) = packages/design-tokens motion.shimmer (shadcn's `shimmer` utility), copied here because the SDK imports nothing from the app (src/text-shimmer.test.ts keeps them equal). The glyphs are filled with a linear gradient at 90deg + `angleDeg` (CSS angle: 90deg = left → right): base = the text colour, highlight (dark mode) = the text colour in OKLCH at lightness min(1, max(`highlightLightnessMin`, L + `highlightLightnessBoost`)), same a/b, alpha min(1, alpha + `highlightAlphaBoost`); light mode = the text colour at alpha × `lightAlphaFactor`; mid = the 50% OKLab mix of the two, alpha-premultiplied. Stops: base @ 50% - spread, mid @ 50% - spread/2, highlight @ 50%, mid @ 50% + spread/2, base @ 50% + spread (spread = `spreadPx`). The gradient is 200% of the text box width + 2 × spread wide and slides linearly from CSS background-position `100% 0` (its right edge on the box's right edge) to `0 0` (its left edge on the box's left edge) over `durationMs`, forever; rtl reverses. Reduced motion = the plain text. src/text-shimmer.ts textShimmer(colour, dark) is the reference (the Rust core `text_shimmer`, FFI `text_shimmer_json`); fixtures/text-shimmer.json locks the colours.

voiceWave.$comment: NEW-77: the VoiceWave native (the EXP-1268 draft made exact): a microphone or speaker level drawn as three closed polar waves around one optional centre child. Per ring k (0 outer, 1 mid, 2 inner): r(t) = size × radius[k] + Σ_j amp_k / (j + 1) × band(k, j) × sin(harmonics[k][j] × t + (phase0[k] + phase) × (j + 1)), t = 2π i / steps for i = 0..steps (the last point repeats the first), x = size/2 + r cos t, y = size/2 + r sin t (y down). amp_k = ringAmp[k] × size / 200 × (activity listening | speaking: ampBase + ampLevel × level; thinking: thinkingAmp; idle | muted: 0). band(k, j) = bands[(3k + j) mod len] clamped to 0..1, or 1 when bands is empty or the activity is thinking; level is clamped to 0..1 and only the first maxBands bands count. phase = the elapsed seconds × phaseSpeed (rad/s) while listening, thinking or speaking; 0 when idle or muted and under reduced motion. Each ring is filled with its part colour at fillAlpha[k] and stroked at strokeAlpha[k], width max(1, strokeWidth[k] × size / 200); the root recipe's opacity applies to the whole wave. THE CHILD RULE: the core lays the one child out centred in the box at its own size (flex, centre, centre); childSize = childScale × size (lg and xl: childScaleLarge; 0 at `sm`, below 40 px); the painter draws the child scaled about the box centre by min(1, childSize / the child's longer edge), never up, and at childSize 0 keeps it in the tree but paints nothing (no hit target, hidden from assistive tech). voiceWaveChildBox(size, child) is that box; the fixture's `child` cases lock it and every painter measures its drawn child against them. src/voice-wave.ts voiceWave(...) is the reference (the Rust core `voice_wave`, FFI `voice_wave_json`); fixtures/voice-wave.json locks the points. VAPP-162: this is `variant: ring` (the default); `variant: bars` is the level meter of `bars` below (same activity, level, bands and phase inputs).

bars.$comment: VAPP-162: the `bars` variant (a horizontal level meter, no child; a child is kept in the tree but never painted, like `sm`): `count` rounded vertical bars side by side, sized per `sizes[size]` = {height, barWidth, gap} (the root box = count × barWidth + (count − 1) × gap wide, `height` tall: the root recipe's `variant: bars` rules). Bar i (0-based): drive d = listening | speaking: (ampBase + ampLevel × level) / (ampBase + ampLevel); thinking: thinkingAmp / (ampBase + ampLevel); idle | muted: 0; band b = bands[i mod len] clamped (1 when bands is empty or thinking); envelope e = 1 − envelope × |2i / (count − 1) − 1| (the middle bars stand tallest); shape s = 0.5 + 0.5 × sin(shapeFreq × i + phase × (1 + (i mod 3) × 0.5)) with the ring's phase (voiceWavePhase: 0 when idle, muted or under reduced motion = a static meter); fraction f = minFraction + (1 − minFraction) × d × b × e × (shapeBase + (1 − shapeBase) × s); the bar is height × f tall (rounded to 0.01), centred vertically (y = (height − h) / 2), at x = i × (barWidth + gap), corner radius barWidth / 2, filled with the `bar` part colour at the root recipe's opacity. voiceWaveBars(input) is the reference; fixtures/voice-wave.json `bars` cases lock it.

qrCode.$comment: VAPP-162: the QrCode native. THE MATRIX COMES FROM THE CORE: src/qr-code.ts qrMatrix(value, level) (a port of Project Nayuki's QR Code generator, MIT: byte mode over the value's UTF-8 bytes, the smallest version 1–40 that fits at the given ECC level, the level kept exact (no boost), the mask with the lowest penalty) → {size n, rows: n strings of '1' (dark) / '0' (light)}, no quiet zone; the Rust core ports it and fixtures/qr-code.json locks every matrix bit. An empty value, or one longer than maxValueBytes UTF-8 bytes at level L (fewer at higher levels: whatever version 40 holds), has NO matrix (`qrMatrix` returns null): the painter shows the plate empty with the label, never throws. PAINT: the root is a column (centred, gap labelGap) of the plate and the label. The plate is `size` px square (the prop, default 160) with radius = the plate recipe's borderRadius; it holds the matrix inside a quiet zone of quietZone modules on every side, so module = size / (n + 2 × quietZone) px (fractional; painters snap module edges to device pixels, never round the module itself, so the code keeps its exact outer size). DARK MODULES ON A LIGHT PLATE ALWAYS: of the two resolved recipe colours (plate and module) the lighter one (higher relative luminance) fills the plate and the darker one the modules, so a dark theme still scans. The label (when given) is a caption Text, muted, centred, under the plate, and the accessibility label of the img.

qrScanner.$comment: VAPP-162: the QrScanner native = the VIEWFINDER CHROME; THE CAMERA IS HOST-OWNED (like FileUpload's bytes). The renderer asks its host for a camera feed through a RENDERER-LEVEL hook each lane defines in its own package API (never catalog/host.json): React/Solid/element a `qrScanner` host option, SwiftUI an environment value, Compose a CompositionLocal, gpui a host trait; the host shows its live feed inside `feed`, decodes codes of the given `formats` and reports a decoded string, which the renderer dispatches as `scanned {value}` (once per distinct value until the value changes or the scanner re-mounts; `disabled` stops reporting). Geometry: the root is a column (centred, gap hintGap); the viewfinder is a square (aspectRatio 1) as wide as the root up to maxWidth px, radius = the viewfinder recipe's borderRadius, clipping; `feed` fills it (the host's video; without one the `feed` recipe colour at feedAlpha alpha); four `corner` brackets sit at the inside corners, each two strokes cornerLength px long and cornerStroke px wide in the corner recipe colour (rounded caps, the outer edge following the viewfinder radius); the `scanLine` is a scanLineHeight px bar inset scanLineInset px from the left and right edges, sweeping top → bottom → top over sweepMs (ease standard, alternate) while a feed shows; reduce motion (or disabled) = the line static at the vertical centre. No host camera = no feed and no line: the `placeholderIcon` (concept ui-scan = Lucide scan-line) placeholderIconSize px centred in the placeholderIcon colour and the built-in string `cameraUnavailable` as a caption under it. The `hint` (when given) is a muted Text centred under the viewfinder.
